paras: The Portsmouth peace conference hotel bellhop incident was a confrontation in late August 1905 at the New Hampshire hotel housing the Russo-Japanese peace conference, in which a guest from Kentucky threatened to cut out the "black heart" of a Black bellhop and began to attack him. Four men pulled the man off, no injury was reported, and the New York Sun told the story as a joke about a near "race war."

The Sun's correspondent at the conference wrote a light column about the hotel, observing that "you can't have so many races and nations mixed up in one hotel without some clash or conflict." According to the column, one of the hotel's Black bellhops had found the decoration of a fraternal order in the hall and was wearing it.

On the evening before the column was written, a "large Kentuckian" who belonged to the order saw the decoration and demanded it, "adding something about cutting a black heart out." When the bellhop refused, the Kentuckian started toward him, and "it took four men to pry him off." The bellhop then told him that he would have handed it over had he been asked "as though I was a human being and not a mere incumbrance." The Kentuckian replied that "this is sure Yankee land" and was led away.
No arrest, complaint or other consequence appears in the coverage.

The only original account ran in the Sun of New York on August 27, 1905, among anecdotes about the envoys and the hotel staff. The column treated the clash as comedy, calling the bellhop "the emancipated Ethiopian," describing the attack as an attempt "to violate the fifteenth amendment," and mocking the bellhop's reply as "Harvard English," while also making the Kentuckian a figure of fun out of place in the North. Southern papers reprinted the passage under the headline "The Comical Side of Portsmouth Conference": the Louisville Courier-Journal ran it on a humor page on September 4, and the Columbia Herald of Tennessee on September 8.
No report of the incident was found in the Black press.

accounts.label: New York Sun conference correspondent
accounts.gist: A Kentuckian at the conference hotel demanded his order's decoration from a Black bellhop with a threat to cut out his 'black heart', began to attack him when refused, and was pulled off by four men; the bellhop rebuked him and the Kentuckian left complaining that this was 'Yankee land'.

framing.detail: The Sun played the episode for laughs as a near 'race war' in a light hotel column, mocking the bellhop's speech as 'Harvard English' while also making the Kentuckian the butt of the joke as out of place in 'Yankee land'.
The Louisville Courier-Journal ran the passage on its 'ON THE FUNNY BONE' page and the Columbia Herald reprinted it, both under 'The Comical Side of Portsmouth Conference'.

sources.note: Continuation of a light column on the peace-conference hotel; tells of a Kentuckian who threatened and began to attack a Black bellhop over a fraternal decoration until four men pulled him off.
quotes: Last night, for example, we came near to having a race war. A large Kentuckian found one of the negro bellhops wearing the decoration of an order to which the Kentuckians belongs.
The Kentuckian demanded it, adding something about cutting a black heart out. This is New Hampshire, and the emancipated Ethiopian refused.
When the Kentuckian got so he could see, he started to violate the fifteenth amendment. It took four men to pry him off.
"If you had asked me for it as though I was a human being and not a mere incumbrance, sir, you would have received it," said the negro in Harvard English.
